No — `opencode` is not a valid summary provider. That setting will make summary generation fail, not fall back.

**What I verified**

Built a binary against this tree and enumerated the registry's `text_generator` capability:

```
claude-code      text_generator=true  streaming=true
codex            text_generator=true  streaming=false
copilot-cli      text_generator=true  streaming=false
cursor           text_generator=true  streaming=false
gemini           text_generator=true  streaming=false
pi               text_generator=true  streaming=false
factoryai-droid  text_generator=false
opencode         text_generator=false
```

`cmd/entire/cli/agent/opencode/` has no `generate.go` and no `GenerateText` method — the six that do are the only `generate.go` files in the tree. So `agent.AsTextGenerator` returns false for it (`explain_summary_provider.go:289`).

Consequences, both ends:

- **Write path is refused.** Ran it: `entire configure --summarize-provider opencode` → `agent "opencode" does not support summary generation`, exit 1 (`validateSummaryProvider`, called from `updateSummaryGenerationSettings` in `setup.go:236`). So the CLI can't have produced that JSON — it's a hand edit. The interactive picker can't either, since `listEnabledSummaryProviders` filters on the same predicate.
- **Read path is a hard error, not a fallback.** `resolveCheckpointSummaryProvider` → `ensureSummaryProviderPresent` (`explain_summary_provider.go:319`) returns `agent opencode does not support summary generation` and the command stops. It never picks a working provider instead. (Read from code — I couldn't exercise it end-to-end without a real checkpoint; `explain --generate` and `dispatch generate` both hit earlier gates in my scratch repo.)

The documented set matches: README:612 lists `claude-code`, `codex`, `copilot-cli`, `cursor`, `gemini`, `pi`, as does the `--summarize-provider` flag help.

**Two things worth knowing**

`.entire/settings.json` in this worktree has no `summary_generation` block at all, so that snippet isn't from here — if it's a proposed edit, drop it or pick one of the six; if it's from another repo, that repo's `explain --generate` is currently broken for everyone who clones it, since a committed project setting fails closed for all readers.

The escape hatch, if you specifically want opencode doing the summarizing: an external `entire-agent-opencode` plugin that declares `text_generator` in its `info` output would satisfy `summary_generation.provider: "opencode-ish-name"` — but it needs the `external_agents` grant in an untracked `.entire/settings.local.json`, and per `discoverSummaryProviderIfMissing` a committed provider name pointing at an external plugin is deliberately blocked without it.

Traced every write path. **No version of the CLI can have written it** — it's a hand edit.

**The two writers, both gated**

1. `entire configure --summarize-provider opencode` → `validateSummaryProvider` (`setup.go:236`) rejects it. Confirmed by running it: exit 1. There's even a test pinning this — `TestConfigureCmd_SummarizeProvider_InvalidProvider` (`setup_test.go:4444`) uses `"opencode"` as its canonical invalid value.
2. `persistSummaryProviderSelection` (`explain_summary_provider.go:349`), which backs the picker and the non-interactive auto-select, can only ever receive a name that came out of `listEnabledSummaryProviders` — and that filters on `agent.AsTextGenerator`. I checked the filter's age: it's in the feature's **first** commit, `d20405606` (2026-04-08), so no older release auto-wrote it either. `git log -S` on the validation strings turns up only the four commits that built the feature. And `agent/opencode/generate.go` has never existed on any ref, so opencode was never briefly capable.

Nothing else writes the key. `dispatch`, `runner setup`, and `runner tune` all *read* through the same resolver.

**The likely confusion, and it's a real one**

`opencode` is a valid value for `entire enable --agent` (README:383) and for `E2E_AGENT` — same registry key, same spelling. Two settings share one name namespace but have different capability requirements, so someone running opencode as their coding agent writes their agent's name into `summary_generation.provider` and it looks right. README:618 says the opposite outright (`opencode` and `factoryai-droid` cannot generate summaries), but that's a README line, not something the tool says at the moment of the mistake. Given the CLI refuses the value, my guess is their agent edited the file — an LLM asked to "set the summary provider" will reach for the agent name it knows itself by.

**Why it survived unnoticed**

- Load-time `SummaryGenerationSettings.Validate()` (`settings.go:282`) only catches *model without provider*. An unsupported provider name passes.
- Neither `entire status` nor `entire doctor` mentions summary generation at all — I grepped both.
- So it sits silent until `explain --generate` / `dispatch` / `runner tune` actually runs, and the error then is `agent opencode does not support summary generation` — which names no alternative. The zero-candidates error one branch away *does* list all six.

If it's in `.entire/settings.json` rather than `settings.local.json` and committed, it's broken for everyone who clones, since a project-layer provider fails closed for all readers.

Two small fixes worth making, if you want them: have that error list the six valid providers the way the zero-candidates one does, and have `doctor` check the configured provider resolves. Say the word and I'll do either.

Yes — but that's already today's behaviour, not something my fix would introduce. Verified in a scratch repo with exactly that settings file:

```
$ entire runner setup -y
```

`-y` is `--yes` → `setupModeAdapt`, which is a `needsProvider()` mode, so `runner_setup.go:233` calls `resolveDispatchSummaryProvider` with an empty override → falls into the settings path → `ensureSummaryProviderPresent` → that error.

**The quoting identifies the source.** Two different functions produce nearly the same sentence:

| what you ran | message | function |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `runner setup -y` (provider from settings) | `agent opencode does not support summary generation` | `ensureSummaryProviderPresent` (`%s`) |
| `runner setup -y --agent opencode` | `agent "opencode" does not support summary generation` | `validateSummaryProvider` (`%q`) |

So if what you were shown is the unquoted form, it came from the settings file, not from an `--agent` flag — which lines up with the provenance conclusion.

My proposed fix only changes the wording, e.g. `agent opencode does not support summary generation; pick one of claude-code, codex, copilot-cli, cursor, gemini, pi, or an external entire-agent-* plugin declaring text_generator`. It still fails — nothing makes opencode able to generate text.

**Separate thing that run exposed:** the scaffold happens before provider resolution, so the command wrote six runner files and *then* exited 1. Re-running doesn't duplicate them but fails identically, so you're left in a state where the runners exist untailored and every retry errors until the setting is fixed. The code deliberately resolves the provider "before the gather" (comment at `runner_setup.go:227`) so a failure doesn't land after seconds of waiting — but ten lines earlier a comment draws the line harder for `--agent`: *"Before the scaffold: a usage error must not leave files behind."* An unusable configured provider is knowable before any write, so it arguably belongs on the same side of that line. Defensible either way — creating the defaults is real work the user asked for — but it's an inconsistency against the file's own stated rule, and probably the more annoying half of what your user hit.

Re-verified 2026-09-09 by running each and reading the failure output.

**Pair 1 — expectation composed from `t.TempDir()`** (the mechanism as originally described):

**Pair 2 — the vouch KEY does not match, so the feature is silently off:**

- `TestCheckAgentDirSymlinks_ScansBeneathAVouchedLink`
- `REDACTED`

These compose **no** path expectation at all — they assert on the literals `"FOLLOWING SYMLINKS"`, `".claude/skills"`, `"SYMLINKS PRESENT"`.
